# Vendoring `rars`

`vendor/rars/` is a curated copy of the `rars` crate from our perf fork of
[bitplane/rars](https://github.com/bitplane/rars). It is **not** a git subtree
or submodule — it is a mirrored subset, produced by
[`sync-from-fork.sh`](sync-from-fork.sh).

Upstream-tracking policy is FREEZE + cherry-pick: watch the fork for decoder
fixes, port selectively, re-run the gates, then re-vendor.

## What is vendored

| Path | Source in fork | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/**` | `crates/rars/src/**` | exact mirror (`rsync --delete`) |
| `tests/fixtures/**` | `crates/rars/tests/fixtures/**` | **exact mirror — all of it** |
| `COPYING` | **not synced - ours** | states this fork's MIT OR Apache-2.0 and why; see below |
| `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE` | **not synced - ours** | the two texts upstream does not ship |
| `Cargo.toml` | `crates/rars/Cargo.toml` | **hand-maintained, see below** |

Not vendored: `tests/*.rs` (fork integration tests — we run only the inline
`--lib` tests), `benches/`, `fuzz/`, `python/`, `scripts/`, `target/`.

## Why `tests/fixtures/**` must always come along

The rars unit tests live **inline** in `src/lib.rs` and load inputs via
`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/tests/fixtures/rar15_40/...`. If any referenced
fixture is missing, `cargo test -p rars --lib` fails with `NotFound` on a clean
checkout.

This exact bug shipped once: an earlier sync copied `src/` but dropped
`tests/fixtures/`, and it was hotfixed by hand-vendoring only the two fixtures
the then-current tests happened to read. Hand-picking fixtures re-introduces the
same fragility — the next inline test that references a third fixture breaks
again. So the sync mirrors the **whole** fixtures tree; do not trim it to a
subset.

## Re-vendoring to a newer fork rev

```sh
# 1. Sync src/ + tests/fixtures/ + COPYING from your fork checkout.
RARS_FORK=~/path/to/rars ./vendor/rars/sync-from-fork.sh

# 2. Reconcile Cargo.toml BY HAND *only if* the fork's [dependencies] changed.
#    The vendored manifest deliberately differs from the fork's:
#      - de-workspaced deps (concrete versions, not `.workspace = true`)
#      - version = "0.4.6+nzbfast"
#      - [lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny" (was forbid until the NEON
#        blake2sp entry, 22 Aug 2026), unused_must_use = "deny"
#      - no [dev-dependencies], no [[bench]] (not vendored)
#    The script never overwrites Cargo.toml, so it survives a re-sync.

# 3. Gate: must stay green.
cargo test -p rars --lib

# 4. Commit.
git add -A vendor/rars
git commit -m "vendor/rars: sync to fork rev <rev>"
```

## Local divergences (re-apply after every sync)

`sync-from-fork.sh` mirrors `src/**` with `rsync --delete`, so anything we
change under `src/` is GONE the moment someone re-vendors. Keep the ledger
below current, and walk it after every sync. Each entry names a marker
comment carrying the same date, so `git grep 'nzbfast-local change'` under
`vendor/rars/src` finds what should be here.

| 2026-09-02 | RAR 5 extraction retains one positional file handle per decoder session/member-pool worker and reuses it for consecutive member ranges, instead of reopening and seeking the same volume for every member. The cache holds only one volume at a time (the pool is capped at eight workers), so descriptor use remains O(workers), never O(volumes); every range reader tracks an explicit logical cursor. It is explicitly cleared before every progress watermark that promises a volume can be deleted, so an open handle cannot pin reclaimed disk space. Memory and growing-stream sources are unchanged, and a short file range still fails with `UnexpectedEof`. Two 20-pair runs over a real RAR 5 CRC-only STORE archive with 10,000 distinct 4 KiB members measured 0.1155 -> 0.015 s and 0.114 -> 0.017 s medians (6.7-7.7x); an exact-copy A/A control differed by 1 ms (0.1205 vs 0.1195 s), and a one-member 1 GiB STORE control was flat within noise (0.102 vs 0.103 s). | `src/source.rs`, `src/rar50.rs`, `src/rar50/extract.rs` |

Existing bucket metadata supplies decode indexes and reconstructs `(code, length)` for the writer, so encoder output and malformed-code errors stay unchanged. Construction places symbols directly into their canonical buckets instead of allocating sortable records. New tests pin scattered multi-length codes, encoder lookup and missing-symbol errors, long-code fallback, the largest RAR5/RAR7 symbol, and refusal rather than truncation outside `u16`. A directional exact-base M1 race moved the 400-member compressed shape about 2% and left the large-member shape inside timing noise; embedding the 2 KiB primary LUT in the table was separately measured neutral and is not retained. | `src/codec/rar50.rs` |
| 2026-09-02 | The non-solid RAR 5 member pool claims adjacent tiny members in adaptive batches of at most eight, amortising its shared work-channel and byte-budget locks. It preserves at least eight batches per worker and limits each batch to one worker's share of the 64 MiB in-flight budget; a single oversized member still advances alone, and checked addition fails closed on hostile size totals. Tiny compressed-member runs improved about 35-40%, while 64-member and 1 MiB-member controls selected batches of one and remained flat. | `src/rar50/extract.rs` |
| 2026-09-03 | Tiny RAR 5 member-pool work ranges (at most eight members and 32 KiB decoded in total) remain grouped on the worker result channel. The coordinator keeps one in-order cursor and stores out-of-order results by batch start, reducing channel receives and reorder-tree operations from once per member to once per batch on the measured 8 x 4 KiB shape. Larger work ranges publish allocation-free singleton packets as each member finishes, avoiding head-of-line delay behind the range's remaining decodes. Member results remain in archive order, decoded bytes retain the existing global in-flight byte charge, and checked size addition makes overflow select the singleton path. | `src/rar50/extract.rs` |
| 2026-09-02 | Tiny file-backed payload ranges (at most 8 KiB) share a 192 KiB forward read-ahead window in each bounded extraction-worker cache. Live readers own their window through `Arc`; an idle cache reuses the allocation without re-zeroing it. A failed speculative read is retried over the required prefix, optional-tail failures are not exposed as member failures or cached as EOF, and truncation still reports `UnexpectedEof`. A 51-run rotating exact-base M1 race measured about 17% less wall time on 10,000 distinct 4 KiB STORE members and 9% on an independent 2,048-member 8 KiB shape. The initially tested 16 KiB boundary was 1.6% slower on that host despite winning locally, so it is deliberately bypassed; 16/32 KiB, one-member 1 GiB, memory, and growing-stream paths remain on the direct reader. Retained memory is 192 KiB per active session/worker, at most about 1.5 MiB for the capped pool. | `src/source.rs` |
| 2026-09-03 | Parallel RAR 5 block tapes return their payload, literal, packed-op, and out-of-band filter vector capacities to the scanner through a bounded, non-blocking recycle channel. Workers also borrow rather than clone each cached nested decode-table `Arc`. Zero LUT entries remain untouched for canonical fallback. A boundary regression test pins that the handoff consumes exactly one code. | `src/codec/rar50.rs` |

The boundary/fallback test derives its long-code width from this constant. | `src/codec/rar50.rs` |

Exhaustive tests cover every length through 64 at distances 16, 17, 31, 64 and 127. In position-balanced M1 product races the isolated change reduced solid, RAR7-dictionary and large mixed extraction by 4.5-5.9%, and its combination with the MATCH dispatch row below reduced them by 7.0-9.6%; the 400-member shape was neutral. | `src/codec/rar50.rs` |
| 2026-09-03 | The flat RAR 5 short-match path performs its first 16-byte stride unconditionally. Decoded match lengths are at least two, so the old zero-length branch ran on every real fast-path match but was never taken. ## Deep gate before a release (decoder changes especially)

The `--lib` gate above and the fuzzers use small inputs, so they are blind to
size-dependent decode bugs: back-references reaching past the streaming window
(>64 MiB), solid cross-member history, and volume-split members only appear in
large real archives. The fork carries a real-`rar` round-trip rig for exactly
these axes at `crates/rars/tests/real_archive_diff.rs`. It is NOT vendored (a
`tests/*.rs` file) and needs a local `rar` 7.x, so run it in the fork checkout
before cutting a release or dropping the external `unrar` fallback:

```sh
cargo test -p rars --test real_archive_diff -- --ignored --nocapture
```

It builds ~76 MiB archives across RAR5/RAR7 dictionary sizes (128 MiB..1 GiB),
solid multi-file sets, and multivolume splits, and asserts rars decodes each
byte-for-byte. This is what would have caught the 64 MiB streaming-window cap.

The whole export ships in the public repo (`vendor` is in
`packaging/PUBLIC_MANIFEST`; `/vendor/` is leak-scan-exempt as third-party
source), which satisfies build-from-source.
